title: Common Cooking Problems & Fixes
description: Practical fixes for the most common things that go wrong in the kitchen, grouped by category.

fixes: Add an acid like lemon juice or vinegar to balance it
Stir in a peeled, raw potato and simmer a few minutes, then remove it -- it absorbs some salt
Dilute with unsalted stock, water, or cream, then adjust other seasoning
Simmer uncovered to reduce and concentrate it
Whisk in a cornstarch slurry (1 tbsp cornstarch + 1 tbsp cold water) a little at a time
Whisk in a small knob of beurre manié (equal parts softened butter and flour)

problems.problem: Cream or egg-based sauce curdled or broke
fixes: Remove from heat immediately and whisk in a splash of cold cream or milk
Blend with an immersion blender to re-emulsify
For next time: temper eggs by whisking in a little hot liquid before adding them back to the pot
Whisk vigorously and continuously while adding the thickener
Strain the finished gravy through a fine sieve
Use a blender or immersion blender to smooth it out
Add salt gradually and taste as you go
Add acid (lemon, vinegar) to brighten the flavour
Add more aromatics (garlic, herbs) or a splash of fish sauce/soy sauce for savoury depth
Check your oven temperature with a separate thermometer -- ovens often run cool
Avoid opening the oven door during the first two-thirds of baking
Don't overmix the batter or use too much leavening, both trap excess air that later collapses
Reduce baking time slightly and check doneness a few minutes early next time
Measure flour by spooning it into the cup and levelling it, not scooping directly, which packs in too much
Add a simple syrup brush or extra fat next time to compensate

problems.problem: Cookies spread too much and went flat
fixes: Chill the dough for at least 30 minutes before baking
Make sure butter isn't too warm or melted when creaming with sugar
Add a little more flour if the dough seems too soft
Check that your yeast is still active -- proof it in warm water with a pinch of sugar; it should foam within 10 minutes
Make sure the liquid wasn't hot enough to kill the yeast (aim for lukewarm, about 105-110°F/40-43°C)
Give it more time in a warm, draft-free spot
Knead longer to develop more gluten structure
Allow a full first and second rise rather than rushing
Don't add too much flour -- sticky dough is normal for many bread recipes

problems.problem: Pastry or pie crust came out tough
fixes: Handle the dough as little as possible to avoid overworking the gluten
Keep the butter cold throughout -- chill the dough again if it warms up
Use ice water, added a little at a time
Chill the bowl, beaters, and cream in the freezer for 10-15 minutes first
Make sure the cream has enough fat content (heavy/whipping cream, not light cream)
Don't overwhip past soft-to-firm peaks or it will turn grainy and then to butter
Match the cooking method to the cut -- tougher cuts need low, slow, moist cooking (braising), not quick high heat
Slice against the grain when serving
Let it rest 5-10 minutes after cooking so juices redistribute
Use a meat thermometer and pull it a few degrees before your target temperature -- it keeps cooking while resting
Avoid pressing down on meat while it cooks, which squeezes out juices
Brine or marinate beforehand for cuts prone to drying out, like chicken breast

problems.problem: Fried food came out soggy, not crispy
fixes: Make sure the oil is hot enough before adding food (test with a small piece first)
Don't overcrowd the pan -- fry in batches so the oil temperature doesn't drop
Drain on a wire rack, not paper towels, so steam escapes instead of softening the crust

problems.problem: Fish is sticking to the pan
fixes: Make sure the pan and oil are properly preheated before adding the fish
Pat the fish completely dry first
Don't move it too early -- it releases naturally once a crust forms
Use less water next time, or rinse the rice first to remove excess surface starch
Don't stir rice while it cooks -- it releases starch and makes it gummy
Let it rest, covered and off heat, for 10 minutes after cooking to finish steaming evenly

problems.problem: Rice came out undercooked or crunchy
fixes: Add a little more water and continue cooking, covered, on low heat
Make sure the pot had a tight-fitting lid to trap steam
Give it the full recommended cooking time before checking
Don't overcook -- test frequently towards the end
Blanch briefly, then shock in ice water to stop the cooking and lock in colour and texture
Cut pieces more evenly so they cook at the same rate

problems.problem: Pickles came out soft instead of crisp
fixes: Use a properly balanced salt-to-vinegar brine ratio
Start with the freshest possible produce -- older vegetables have less natural crispness to retain
Keep the brine cold and avoid over-processing if canning
